extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of American literature (undergraduate/secondary-level)
extracted.subtask_description: Reading-guide style study prompts and analytical questions for students analyzing early 20th-century American authors and poets; focuses on themes, style, sources, and comparisons with contemporaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willa Cather — realism
rubrics_metrics.description: her realism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: 'Miss Cather's special field is the pioneer life of immigrants in the Middle West. Points to be considered are: (1) her realism; (2) her detachment or objectivity; (3) her sympathy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Willa Cather — detachment/objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: her detachment or objectivity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: consider Cather's detachment or objectivity when studying her portrayal of pioneer immigrant life in the Middle West.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willa Cather — sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: her sympathy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: consider Cather's sympathy as a key feature in her treatment of characters and material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willa Cather — distinguishing qualities among women novelists
rubrics_metrics.description: In what other respects does she stand out among the leading women novelists of today?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt to identify other distinctive qualities (beyond realism, objectivity, sympathy) that separate Cather from her contemporaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willa Cather — value of material
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the value of her material?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt to evaluate the worth and significance of Cather's chosen subject matter (pioneer immigrant life).

rubrics_metrics.name: Willa Cather — comparative study
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare her studies with those of Cahan (q.v.), Cournos (q.v.), and Tobenkin (q.v.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides comparative analysis across authors treating similar immigrant/pioneer material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winston Churchill — analyze moral earnestness and national feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflect on Churchill's combination of heroic color and moral earnestness and how much he owes to the element injected into American life by Theodore Roosevelt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted guidance (Carl Van Doren): 'To reflect a little upon this combination of heroic color and moral earnestness is to discover how much Mr. Churchill owes to the element injected into American life by Theodore Roosevelt.... Like him Mr. Churchill has habitually moved along the main lines of national feeling—believing in America and democracy with a fealty unshaken by any adverse evidence and delighting in the American pageant with a gusto rarely modified by the exercise of any critical intelligence.' Also consider his 'genuine earnestness', his success in holding audiences, and whether he acts like a philosopher or seer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theodore Dreiser — sources of strength and weakness (Zola and journalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe that his attitude toward life and his general method derive from Zola; that his materials are drawn from his extensive and varied experience as a journalist; and that these facts are exemplified in 'Twelve Men' as 'human documents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: 'As Mr. Dreiser is considered by many critics the novelist of biggest stature as yet produced by America, the nature and sources of his strength and of his weakness deserve careful analysis. Observe (1) that his attitude toward life and his general method derive from Zola; (2) that his materials are drawn from his extensive and varied experience as a journalist; (3) that these two facts are exemplified in brief in his biographical studies, 'Twelve Men,' which are "human documents."'

rubrics_metrics.name: Theodore Dreiser — loss and gain during silence
rubrics_metrics.description: Note the dates of 'Sister Carrie' and of 'Jennie Gerhardt', and work out Dreiser's loss and gain during the long period of silence between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt to chart artistic development across publication gaps and assess changes in craft or perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theodore Dreiser — read 'Hey, Rub-a-Dub-Dub' for author's attitude
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Hey, Rub-a-Dub-Dub' should be read for its revelation of his attitude toward humanity and of his failure to think out a point of view; note his admission: "I am one of those curious persons who cannot make up their minds about anything."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the work to gauge Dreiser's moral/psychological stance and consistency of viewpoint; evaluate how this affects his fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theodore Dreiser — types of material he succeeds with
rubrics_metrics.description: With what types of material does Mr. Dreiser succeed best? Why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical prompt to identify subject-matter best suited to Dreiser's methods and strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theodore Dreiser — discuss style across topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss Dreiser's style in connection with the following topics: (1) economy; (2) realism; (3) suggestion; (4) taste; (5) rhythmic beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured checklist of stylistic dimensions to evaluate Dreiser's prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theodore Dreiser — representation of American life
rubrics_metrics.description: How far does Mr. Dreiser represent American life? Do you think his work will be for some time the best that we can do in literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad evaluative question about Dreiser's cultural representativeness and long-term literary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theodore Dreiser — consult Van Doren for further points
rubrics_metrics.description: Read Mr. Van Doren's article for suggestions of other points for discussion; the passage beginning 'Not the incurable awkwardness of his style...' is especially significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages reading contemporary criticism (Van Doren) to supplement student analysis; quoted passage highlights Dreiser's strengths and defects (style awkwardness, occasional verbosity, cosmic philosophizing, ennobling opportunities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adelaide Crapsey — remember versification theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Miss Crapsey's theories of versification should be remembered in studying her forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt to apply Crapsey's theoretical work (structure of English verse, invention of the 'cinquain') when analyzing her poems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adelaide Crapsey — verbal economy
rubrics_metrics.description: What is to be said of her verbal economy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical prompt to assess concision and economy of language in Crapsey's poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adelaide Crapsey — compare with Emily Dickinson
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare her verses with those of Emily Dickinson; carried out in detail, it suggests interesting points of difference as well as of resemblance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides comparative analysis to reveal both affinities and contrasts in form, tone, and technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: T. S. Eliot — source of poetry: life vs. literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Is Mr. Eliot's poetry derived from a keen sense of life experienced or from literature? What echoes of earlier poets do you find in his work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompts examination of influences and whether Eliot's poems grow from lived experience or literary precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: T. S. Eliot — evidences of distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the adjective 'distinguished' apply to his work? What are the sources of his distinction? What evidences of fresh vision of old things do you find? of unexpected and true associations and contrasts? of a delicate sense for essential details that make a picture? of the power of suggestive condensation? of ability to get an emotional effect through irony?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist of specific qualities to look for when judging Eliot's claim to distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: T. S. Eliot — consider quoted method statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider Eliot's own quoted method: 'The contemplation of the horrid or sordid by the artist is the necessary and negative aspect of the impulse toward beauty.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the quotation to illuminate Eliot's aesthetic stance and to frame readings of his poems.

rubrics_metrics.name: T. S. Eliot — study management of verse
rubrics_metrics.description: It is interesting to make a special study of Mr. Eliot's management of verse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directive to focus on form and technical handling of verse (lineation, rhythm, enjambment, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: T. S. Eliot — possible temperamental defects
rubrics_metrics.description: What, if any, temperamental defect is likely to interfere with his development?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt to consider non-technical personal/temperamental factors that might affect Eliot's future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: John Gould Fletcher — read prefaces for theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the prefaces to 'Irradiations' and 'Goblins and Pagodas' for Mr. Fletcher's theory of poetry before you read the poems themselves. Has he succeeded in making the arts of painting and music do service to poetry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional: consult authorial prefatory material to understand theoretical aims and judge success in synthesizing other arts with poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: John Gould Fletcher — evaluate Aiken's criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: After reading the poems, consider the justice or injustice of Mr. Aiken's criticism: 'It is a sort of absolute poetry, a poetry of detached waver and brilliance, a beautiful flowering of language alone--a parthenogenesis, as if language were fertilized by itself rather than by thought or feeling. Remove the magic of phrase and sound and there is nothing left: no thread of continuity, no thought, no story, no emotion. But the magic of phrase and sound is powerful, and it takes one into a fantastic world.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Aiken's critique as a test-case: determine whether Fletcher's poetry depends primarily on sonic/phrasing effects at the expense of thought or narrative continuity.
